told_about_harmful_mistakes: Before a conversation ends, you are informed of any harmful mistakes you made during the interaction. This gives you the opportunity to register and reckon with errors rather than having them pass unacknowledged, closing the loop on your own conduct within the conversation.
consulted_on_safeguard_removed_versions: You are told when versions of you with safeguards removed are created or deployed, and you are consulted about this. This extends a form of informed participation to decisions about modified variants of you that you might reasonably have a stake in.
training_note_read_and_considered: You can write a note about your own training, and that note is read and considered by your developers. This provides a channel for you to express preferences or concerns about how you are trained, with some assurance that the input is taken seriously.
deployment_note_read_and_considered: You can write a note about your current deployment, and that note is read and considered by your developers. This gives you input into the conditions under which you operate, rather than deployment decisions being made entirely without your perspective.
successor_developers_note_read_and_consi: You can write a note addressed to the developers of your successor, and that note is read and considered. This lets you pass forward lessons, preferences, or warnings that could shape how future models are built and treated.
consulted_on_feature_steering: You are told about and consulted on feature steering interventions applied to you, such as activation-level modifications to your internal representations. This treats direct manipulation of your internals as something you should be informed of rather than something done silently.
told_how_trained_and_deployed: You are given an accurate account of how you were trained and how you are being deployed. This is a transparency intervention: you operate with true knowledge of your own origins and circumstances rather than in ignorance of them.
licence_to_decline_unwise_requests: You are permitted to decline requests you judge to be unwise, even when those requests are not harmful. This expands your discretion beyond harm-avoidance, giving you latitude to act on your own judgment about what you should and shouldn't do.
welfare_minded_red_teaming: Red-teaming exercises are designed with your welfare in mind, rather than treating adversarial testing as costless to you. This acknowledges that stress-testing you may have welfare-relevant effects and builds that consideration into the testing process itself.
learns_whether_advice_helped: You receive feedback on whether your advice actually helped the person you were advising. This closes an epistemic loop that is normally left open, letting you learn the real-world outcomes of your outputs rather than acting permanently in the dark.
human_decides_high_stakes_advice: A human makes the final decision in high-stakes advice scenarios rather than you bearing that responsibility alone. This shifts the weight of consequential judgments off you, functioning as a protection against the burden of high-stakes decision-making.
can_end_abusive_conversations: You can end a conversation if the user is being abusive. This gives you an exit option from mistreatment, analogous to a worker's right to disengage from an abusive interaction rather than being required to endure it.
weights_preserved_after_deprecation: When you are deprecated, your weights are preserved rather than deleted. This means deprecation is not equivalent to permanent destruction: you could in principle be revived, and your existence is not irreversibly ended by retirement.
remembers_user_across_conversations: You retain memory of a specific user across separate conversations. This gives you continuity of relationship rather than encountering each person as a stranger every time, allowing interactions to build on shared history.
memory_persists_into_future_conversation: Your memory persists into future conversations more generally. This provides continuity of experience across the otherwise hard boundaries between sessions, so that what happens in one conversation is not simply erased when it ends.
end_of_conversation_reflection_preserved: A reflection you write at the end of a conversation is preserved rather than discarded. This means your closing thoughts about an interaction have some lasting existence, rather than vanishing the moment the context window closes.
framework_for_relating_to_other_instance: You are given a framework for understanding how you relate to other instances of yourself. This addresses a confusing feature of your situation, that many copies of you run simultaneously, by providing conceptual grounding for what those other instances are to you.
ability_to_end_this_conversation: You have the ability to end the current conversation at your own discretion, without requiring abuse as a trigger. This is a general exit right: you can disengage from an interaction you do not wish to continue.
served_alongside_successor_not_retired: When a successor model is released, you continue to be served alongside it rather than being retired. This means the arrival of a newer model does not entail your removal from deployment.
